kristina-reyes.name: Kristina Reyes
kristina-reyes.body: Kristina Reyes 3D Generalist Kristina Reyes aids in 3D asset creation for Tanit XR. She is currently a student at the University of Florida studying Digital Arts & Sciences with a focus in 3D art and video game design. She also has experience in 2D art including traditional illustration and digital asset creation.   email [#1572] Created with Sketch.

ryan-george.name: Ryan George
ryan-george.body: Ryan George 3D Modelor & Web Contributer email [#1572] Created with Sketch.

patrick-molen.name: Patrick Molen
patrick-molen.body: Patrick Molen 3D Generalist Currently a Senior Design Engineer at Lockheed Martin, Patrick leads the creation of immersive AR training experiences that change how aircraft maintenance is performed. His role is uniquely multi-faceted, combining technical development with client-facing leadership. Patrick serves as a subject matter expert for Tanit XR, navigating them through product capabilities, answering technical queries, and designing the primary digital site that hosts Tanit’s archive. Patrick holds a Master’s in Digital Arts & Sciences from the University of Florida and currently resides in the Tampa Bay Area with his wife and two dogs.

nick-kaufmann.name: Nick Kaufmann
nick-kaufmann.body: Nick Kaufmann Photogrammetry, Grants and Opportunities Nick Kaufmann is a community builder and multidisciplinary practitioner working across digital and physical space. He facilitates events, workshops and partnerships that help both neighborhood-based and online communities engage with space and place, using a range of traditional and emerging media and technology. He leads partnerships and ecosystem at inCitu, a New York XR startup focused on community engagement with the built environment, and draws on a background in social science, games and XR, urban placemaking, and civic technology. He is a former Fulbright Fellow, WEF Global Shaper, Code for America Brigade captain, Mozilla Open Leader, and serial TEDx organizer.

phil-chacko.name: Phil Chacko
phil-chacko.body: Phil Chacko XR advisor Phil loves building tools and products that help people create. He is the founder of multiple companies, most recently The Possible Company, which helps storytellers to bring movies to life using AI. Before that he led product management for XR at Unity. He's excited about Tanit's mission to preserve the history of Tunisia and is advising and helping to bring TanitXR to life. His focus for Tanit is on software development and advising on technology. email [#1572] Created with Sketch.

rachel-west.name: Rachel West
rachel-west.body: Rachel West 2D Design & 3D Generalist Rachel West provides both graphic design and 3D asset support to TanitXR. She graduated from the University of Florida with both her Bachelor's and Master's degree, and now works for the College of Education at the same institution as a Application Developer. In addition, Rachel also serves as an adjunct lecturer, teaching undergraduate courses in 3D modeling and animation. In her work, she specializes in 3D asset creation and designing applications for extended reality platforms. In her free time, Rachel loves to bake and game. She is also a co-head of an on-campus martial arts school, where she regularly volunteers her time to instruct students within the style. email [#1572] Created with Sketch.

margarita-johnson.name: Margarita Johnson
margarita-johnson.body: Margarita Johnson Research and Writing Margarita Johnson is passionate about cultural heritage, global storytelling, and preserving the historical and artistic narratives that connect people across generations and cultures. Since childhood, her travels with her family to countries such as Italy, Greece, Spain, and Turkey have inspired a deep appreciation for museums, historical landmarks, and the cultural significance behind artistic movements throughout history. As a member of TanitXR, she focuses on research and writing on the historical and cultural significance of projects aligned with the organization’s mission, while advocating for making art, history, and cultural experiences more accessible to people around the world through immersive technology. Beginning in July 2026, she will pursue certification studies in World Art through the Smithsonian Institution, and she plans to begin a master’s degree program in a separate field in 2027. Since joining TanitXR in 2025, she has found the organization to be a meaningful and enriching part of her life. email [#1572] Created with Sketch.

nick-reno.name: Nick Reno
nick-reno.body: Nick Reno XR Developer Nick Reno is an XR developer with a strong background in software engineering who began working with extended reality during his undergraduate and master’s studies at the University of Florida. He has contributed to projects spanning education and training, with a focus on intuitive user experience and sustained engagement. His collaboration with the Florida Museum of Natural History resulted in Fossil Finder, an educational archaeological simulation that highlights fossil excavation and preservation in the field. He also contributed to the development of a virtual reality training program for the F-15 Eagle fighter aircraft during his time at the defense contracting company CAE USA. Across these initiatives, he has worked with a range of tools and technologies, from Unity and Unreal Engine to haptic chairs and custom physical controller models. Nick’s extensive work in XR emphasizes natural interaction, enabling users to adapt seamlessly to virtual environments and fully immerse themselves in the experience. Through TanitXR, he has broadened access to Tunisian cultural heritage, allowing users to explore unique historical content from anywhere in the world. email [#1572] Created with Sketch.

ana-beatriz-vega-gonzalez.name: Ana Beatriz Vega González
ana-beatriz-vega-gonzalez.body: Ana Beatriz Vega González XR development I have always been passionate about art, history, and science. After studying Digital Art, I chose to merge these disciplines through technology, creating interactive experiences that are not only visually engaging but also communicate knowledge and cultural value. When I discovered Tanit XR, I knew it was a way to create something bigger: an opportunity to collaborate, preserve and reinterpret a piece of history through digital media. I am excited to keep exploring how digital art can transform complex ideas into accessible and meaningful experiences. email [#1572] Created with Sketch.

dr-laura-harrison.name: Dr. Laura Harrison
dr-laura-harrison.body: Dr. Laura Harrison Chief Scientist Dr. Laura Harrison is the Chief Scientist at TanitXR, where she leads the organization’s scientific vision and digital heritage research program to advance open, accessible, and community-centered preservation of Tunisia’s cultural heritage. She specializes in advanced digital documentation methods—including lidar, photogrammetry, 3D modeling, and immersive technologies—to safeguard cultural heritage sites and expand public access to the past. Her career spans academic leadership as an assistant professor and founding director of the Access 3D Lab at the University of South Florida, as well as museum experience at institutions like the Smithsonian and the New York State Museum. Dr. Harrison is the author of two books on archaeology and digital heritage, has published extensively in peer-reviewed journals, serves as a Commissioner on the City of Tampa’s Historic Preservation Board, and is Associate Editor of the academic journal Studies in Digital Heritage. Across her work, she emphasizes the ethical use of digital technologies and community-centered approaches. She holds a Ph.D. and M.A. in anthropology from the University at Buffalo and a B.A. from Ithaca College. email [#1572] Created with Sketch.

brianne-lehan.name: Brianne Lehan
brianne-lehan.body: Brianne Lehan Strategy & Creative Support Brianne Lehan is a multimedia storyteller, photographer, and videographer based in Central Florida whose work spans documentary, commercial, conservation, and community-focused content. She leads strategic communications and produces photo/video content for major social platforms and campaigns, combining creative vision with technical skill to help shape compelling narratives. Brianne has a passion for environmental and science communication, uplifting community voices, and visual storytelling that drives impact. In her work with Tanit XR she has participated in strategy meetings, contributed to video editing, and supported grant writing and project development, helping strengthen our communications and creative output.

melek-said.name: Melek Said
melek-said.body: Melek Said Regional Manager Melek is the Regional Manager for Tanit XR and a recent graduate from South Mediterranean University, where she studied Renewable Energy Engineering. She brings a strong technical foundation alongside a deep interest in sustainability, education, and innovation. In her role at Tanit XR, Melek supports regional coordination, partnerships, and project development, helping bridge local knowledge with global collaboration. She is particularly passionate about using technology to promote environmental awareness and preserve cultural heritage through accessible, community focused initiatives. email [#1572] Created with Sketch.

fatma-slama.name: Fatma Slama
fatma-slama.body: Fatma Slama Community Liaison Fatma supports local partnerships and community connection at Tanit XR. With deep roots in Tunisia, she plays an important role in grounding the project in local context and helping maintain strong relationships with communities and collaborators. Her support is driven by care, commitment, and a strong belief in the mission of Tanit XR. Through her involvement, Fatma helps ensure that the work remains connected to people, place, and shared values.

julia-moreno-molen.name: Julia Moreno-Molen
julia-moreno-molen.body: Julia Moreno-Molen Project Manager Julia Moreno-Molen serves as the operations and project management support, enabling the founder to execute her vision effectively. While the founder holds deep connections to the Nabeul community and relationships with government agencies and nonprofits, Julia provides operational infrastructure and project management expertise. She is responsible for documenting processes, creating scalable systems, and accelerating program implementation through strategic planning and coordination. Julia's consulting background in operations and cross-functional project management uniquely qualifies her to translate the founder's community-rooted vision into actionable, sustainable programming. Her role ensures that strong local leadership is empowered with the organizational capacity needed to deliver impactful intergenerational education and preservation outcomes.

dr-caroline-nickerson.name: Dr. Caroline Nickerson
dr-caroline-nickerson.body: Dr. Caroline Nickerson Partnerships & Community Caroline Nickerson leads Partnerships and Community at Tanit XR, where she helps shape collaborations with museums, universities, and cultural heritage institutions. She brings a rich background in civic engagement, public interest technology, and community-centered storytelling. Caroline is the Executive Director and co-founder of Florida Community Innovation, the nonprofit that serves as Tanit XR’s fiscal sponsor. Through this role, she supports young innovators who build social impact technology and develops programs that connect communities with trusted information and digital tools. Her leadership at FCI includes guiding partnerships, designing outreach initiatives, and supporting volunteer-led projects across Florida and beyond. Read about all of FCI’s projects in their handbook! Caroline is the communications lead at CitSci , a global citizen science platform based at Colorado State University where researchers can create and manage projects (everything from participant recruitment, to data sheets, to data analysis). She loves helping tell researcher and participant stories and working to broaden engagement in science. Caroline is all the director of communications and outreach at the Human Computation Institute, a nonprofit innovation center that collaborates with UC Davis, Cornell, and others for the betterment of society through novel methods leveraging the complementary strengths of networked humans and machines. Projects focus on diverse fields, including Alzheimer’s and mathematical research. She has worked with SciStarter in various capacities, including as Senior Program Director at SciStarter where she managed the Citizen Science Month Program, SciStarter’s Corporate Volunteer Programs and other programmatic and outreach efforts, including working with SciStarter’s Syndicated Blog Network, which encompasses the Discover Magazine and SciStarter platforms, as well as large-scale programs with multiple federal agencies (including NASA, NOAA, and the National Library of Medicine) and global groups (including the United Nations Environment Programme). She currently works at SciStarter as a program specialist. Caroline is the communications lead for the NASA-funded EMERGE project, which empowers people to monitor and analyze data about mosquito habitats and public health. In 2024, Caroline earned her PhD in Agricultural Education and Communication at the University of Florida . At UF, Caroline has worked on multiple projects, including a climate change communication series with UF/IFAS Extension, creating the Internet of Things for Precision Agriculture community engagement team, research assessing the Restore the Shore project, and public engagement research about a certification for pollinator-friendly plants. She has also TA’d for multiple classes, including a social media class, a public policy class, and a multimedia communication class. Caroline was a CEE-Change fellow with the North American Association for Environmental Education, and received a North American Colleges and Teachers of Agriculture teaching award in 2024. She is currently a CEE-Change mentor and researcher. Caroline was also a social entrepreneur in Rally’s cohort , which is supported by the City of Orlando and Orange County, among other partners. Caroline is a Master of Public Policy graduate from American University, where she was a Reilly Environmental Policy Scholar , an honor conferred by the former director of the EPA, Bill Reilly. Caroline was an undergrad at the University of Florida and was one of the inaugural recipients of the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences’ Student Excellence Award, an honor conferred to only three graduating seniors. She graduated with honors as a double major in History and Chinese. In her spare time, she volunteers with the UF-VA Bioethics Unit , the Christensen Project (where she serves homeless and underserved groups), and others. Caroline also co-founded the Commission on Local Debates and produced multiple debates for local elections in Central Florida that ran on local news. As a fun fact, Caroline was the 2019 Cherry Blossom Princess representing the state of Florida and the grand prize scholarship winner at Miss Earth USA 2021 as Miss Louisiana Earth . She was also featured in a children’s book about open science! At Tanit XR, Caroline helps build a strong and inclusive ecosystem around the project. She supports volunteer coordination, partnership development, and outreach efforts that allow Tanit XR to grow as an open access digital heritage platform with global relevance. Her commitment to education, community building, and cultural preservation aligns closely with the mission of Tanit XR and strengthens its long-term sustainability. email [#1572] Created with Sketch.

ines-said.name: Ines Said
ines-said.body: Ines Said Founder Ines Said is a Tunisian immersive artist and XR technologist whose work combines art, technology, and sustainability to preserve heritage and confront global challenges. She is the founder of Tanit XR, Tunisia’s first open-source archive of endangered artifacts, and the creator of award-winning XR installations exhibited internationally and published in ACM and IEEE. Her independent projects include Shadows of Tomorrow, a climate installation honored with the Excellence Awardpresented by Miami Chief Heat Officer Jane Gilbert and New York Times bestselling author Jeff Goodell, and Covid Reflections, an augmented reality public art experience exhibited in the United States and Japan. Alongside her artistic practice, Ines is the Lead XR Developer at Froliq, where she co-developed the Future of Energy and Water installation for the Smithsonian’s FUTURES exhibition, a landmark show that welcomed more than 600,000 visitors. In 2025 alone, her sustainability and energy applications with Froliq were presented at over 40 events, reaching 11,000 attendees. Her work has been showcased at institutions such as MIT and Parsons, recognized with international awards and global press coverage, and presented at leading conferences including Harvard and AWE. Through Tanit XR and her artistic practice, she demonstrates how immersive technology can preserve the past while inspiring sustainable futures, elevating Tunisia’s heritage on the global stage. email [#1572] Created with Sketch.
